draft.title: Sensitive and critical periods
card: a stretch of time when the brain is especially ready to build a skill, so the skill develops most easily. Learning is still possible after it, but it is usually harder.
a narrow window when certain experiences must occur for a type of development to happen normally. If the window passes, that development may not happen at all.
Language is an example. Young children pick up the sounds and grammar of a language easily, and learning a new language gets harder with age. This fits a sensitive period.
Both periods show that timing matters. Experiences during these times shape the brain more strongly than the same experiences at other times.
draft.remember: Sensitive: easiest time to learn, but later learning is still possible. Critical: a narrow window, and development may be lost if it is missed.

a.q: Which statement best describes a sensitive period?
opts: A time when a skill is easiest to learn, but later learning is possible
A time after which a skill can never be learnt, whatever the effort
A time when genes alone decide how a skill will develop in a child
A time when a skill develops at the same rate as at any other time
a.why: A sensitive period is when the brain is most ready to build a skill, so learning is easiest. Learning later is still possible, which is the difference from a critical period, where missing the window may mean the development does not happen.
a.clue: Think about whether the skill can still be learnt later.

b.q: Tom moves to Melbourne at age 15 and starts learning Italian. He makes steady progress but finds it harder than his young cousin did. Which idea best explains this?
opts: Language learning has a sensitive period that is now past
Language learning has a critical period that is now closed
Tom's genes have stopped him from learning Italian
Tom's environment has no effect on his language learning
b.why: Tom is still making progress, so learning is possible but harder. That fits a sensitive period. A critical period is tempting, but it would mean the development may not happen at all, and Tom is clearly learning.
b.clue: Is Tom still able to learn, or is the window fully shut?
